slides.h1: Everyone at work uses ChatGPT and Claude.
slides.h2: Almost nobody knows what they remember.

slides.title: Your AI has two memories.
boxes: A profile built from your chats. A synthesis, not a transcript.
The current conversation. It degrades as the chat gets long.

slides.title: Long chats start ignoring your instructions.
slides.body: Models pay the most attention to the start and end of a conversation. The middle gets blurry.
slides.fix: Restate the rule right before the task, or start a fresh chat.

slides.title: It remembers wrong or stale things.
slides.body: Any chat can feed your profile. Help a friend with a resume and it might think you're job hunting.
slides.fix: Keep one-offs in Temporary Chat (ChatGPT) or Incognito (Claude). Then edit the memory page.

slides.title: Important context doesn't carry over.
slides.body: Memory keeps highlights, not transcripts. What it considered minor may simply be gone.
slides.fix: Pin must-haves in Custom Instructions (ChatGPT) or a Project (Claude).

slides.title: Deleting a chat does not delete what it learned.
slides.body: True in ChatGPT and Claude, and both vendors document it. Removing the memory is a separate step.

eyebrow: The part that matters at work
slides.title: Private mode is not invisible to your company.
slides.body: On Claude Team and Enterprise plans, incognito chats still follow your org's data retention policy.
slides.aside: Worth knowing what your ChatGPT workspace is set to as well.

slides.title: Ten minutes with your team:
slides.tail: Read what's in there. Fix what's wrong.
